messages.content: Write a recap post about what a team learned at an industry conference. Around 250 words.

Assuming a generic engineering-team context — swap the names for your actual conference and speakers.

---

**What we brought back from KubeCon**

Five of us went. We came back with about four hundred conference-swag stickers and one uncomfortable realization.

The realization: our incident review process is slower than almost everyone we talked to. We'd assumed a 48-hour turnaround on a postmortem was tight. Two separate hallway conversations — one with a team at a payments company, one with a platform group at a retailer we won't name — put their number at same-day, with the write-up drafted while the incident channel is still open. Nobody thought that was heroic. It was just how they worked.

The talks were a mixed bag, honestly. A lot of the keynote material was vendors describing problems we don't have. But Priya's session pick on Wednesday was worth the trip on its own: a walkthrough of how one team cut their build times by deleting tests instead of adding parallelism. They killed 300 tests that had never once failed on a real bug. Build went from 22 minutes to 9.

Sana spent most of Thursday in the eBPF track and has opinions now. Ask her.

What changes for us: we're moving postmortem drafting into the incident itself, starting with the next Sev-2. Marcus is auditing our test suite for the never-failed-once category. And we're sending three people next year instead of five — the value was in the conversations between sessions, and five of us clustered together talked mostly to each other.

Slides and notes are in the shared drive.
